why: Same notions on both sides (B's levelTo f 1 1 is levelMap f 1 by rfl; U¹ = E.lvlSet U 1 in E.shift; sc^k = IsSck), so A ⇒ B is IsSck.shift on the sc-domain U (IsRelOpenInQuadrant.isScDomain) plus IsSc0.levelMap_mapsTo for f(U¹) ⊆ V¹. B ⇒ A fails for a genuine reason: A's conjuncts are stated for arbitrary domains (IsSc0.shift for any U ⊆ E₀, the others for any IsScDomain U such as a closed disc, not relatively open in a partial quadrant), while B only covers relatively open subsets of partial quadrants. Restricted to those domains, IsSc0.shift, IsSck.shift and IsScSmooth.shift follow from B (B_shift_quadrant, B_sc0_shift_quadrant, B_smooth_shift_quadrant, rt_check OK, with V = C' = F₀); IsScDomain.shift is a domain-class fact B does not address (re-proved outright); IsSc1With.shift also names the derivative family levelDeriv D 1, which B's existential IsSc1 does not, but on those domains it follows as well (B_sc1With_shift_quadrant: B's family agrees with levelDeriv D 1 on U₂ by uniqueness of derivatives of f : U₂ → F₀ and density of E₂ in E₁). So the only gap is the domain class. B's extra hypotheses (V relatively open, f(U) ⊆ V) are used only for its MapsTo conjunct.
